description: One acceptance criterion per rule that produces a work item. Written per rule rather than generated per finding, and substituted with the component at publish time. Every rule in the catalogue with a work item type other than 'none' needs an entry here and the contract integrity check fails when one is missing.

rules.shape: Given, when, then, plus an explicit test requirement. The test requirement is separate because 'the flow now has error handling' is a state and 'a deliberate failure reaches the notification channel' is a test, and only the second one catches a handler wired to nothing.
rules.noBoilerplate: A criterion saying 'the finding is resolved' is worse than none. It teaches a team that these work items are generated noise, and after the third one they close the rest without reading them.
rules.substitution: {componentName}, {componentType}, {solutionName}, {tableName}, {evidenceValue} and {count} are replaced at publish time. A placeholder with nothing behind it is dropped with its sentence rather than published as a brace.
rules.theTestIsTheHardPart: Most of these findings sit in code nobody has ever tested. The test requirement is usually the larger half of the estimate and is written first for that reason.

lifecycle.dialogPresent.then: No dialog records remain in the solution, and no security role, form or site map entry refers to one
lifecycle.dialogPresent.testRequirement: Confirm nothing referenced it before deleting. A dialog is unreachable in the interface, so the only way it is still doing anything is through a link somebody built to it.

lifecycle.deprecatedClientApi.given: The web resource {componentName} calling a removed client API
lifecycle.deprecatedClientApi.when: Each call has been replaced with its documented successor
lifecycle.deprecatedClientApi.then: The Power Apps checker reports no deprecated client API findings for this web resource, and every form that loads it behaves as it did
lifecycle.deprecatedClientApi.testRequirement: Open each form the web resource is registered on and exercise the behaviour it controls. A removed API fails silently in some browsers and loudly in others, so a single browser check proves less than it appears to.

lifecycle.classicWorkflowInUse.when: Its replacement is in place and the workflow is deactivated
lifecycle.classicWorkflowInUse.then: The same records are produced, with the same values, for every trigger condition the workflow handled
lifecycle.classicWorkflowInUse.testRequirement: Run both for an agreed period against the same data and compare the output before deactivating the original. A workflow replaced and deactivated in one deployment has no way back inside a change window.

lifecycle.classicWorkflowDormant.given: The classic workflow {componentName}, activated and with no execution recorded in ninety days
lifecycle.classicWorkflowDormant.when: Somebody has established which of the two explanations applies
lifecycle.classicWorkflowDormant.then: Either it is deactivated and deleted, or a defect is raised saying why it should have run and did not
lifecycle.classicWorkflowDormant.testRequirement: Create a record that matches its trigger conditions in a non production environment and watch whether it fires. That answers the question in ten minutes and no amount of reading the definition will.

lifecycle.customWorkflowActivity.given: The custom workflow activity {componentName}, called by at least one activated workflow
lifecycle.customWorkflowActivity.when: Its logic has been moved to a custom API or a plugin and every calling workflow has been repointed
lifecycle.customWorkflowActivity.then: No activated workflow references the activity, and the assembly can be removed without breaking an import
lifecycle.customWorkflowActivity.testRequirement: Exercise every calling workflow end to end against the new implementation. The activity's inputs and outputs are typed differently from a custom API's parameters, and a mapping error here produces a wrong value rather than an error.

lifecycle.rdlReport.when: A decision has been recorded to delete it, rebuild it in Power BI, or replace it with a view
lifecycle.rdlReport.then: The decision names who uses the report and how often, and the replacement produces the same figures for an agreed reporting period
lifecycle.rdlReport.testRequirement: Run the original and the replacement over the same period and reconcile the totals line by line. Reports disagree for reasons nobody predicts, usually a filter on a status nobody documented.

lifecycle.dataflowPresent.when: It has been rebuilt somewhere it can be versioned, or retired
lifecycle.dataflowPresent.then: The destination tables hold the same data after a full cycle, and the new implementation exists in source control
lifecycle.dataflowPresent.testRequirement: Run both against the same source for one full cycle and compare row counts and a sample of values. Also confirm the Dataverse capacity consumption after the change, because that was half the reason for the finding.

architecture.logicSpread.given: The table {tableName}, with logic in {count} different places
architecture.logicSpread.when: The execution order on create and on update has been mapped and the consolidation agreed in that map has been done
architecture.logicSpread.then: The map exists as a document a new developer can read, and the number of distinct mechanisms firing on that table has gone down
architecture.logicSpread.testRequirement: Create, update and delete a record and confirm every expected side effect happens, in the expected order, once. The failure this rule exists for is a side effect happening twice, or not at all, depending on which mechanism ran first.

architecture.proCodeWhereConfigWouldDo.given: The form script {componentName}, doing only visibility and validation
architecture.proCodeWhereConfigWouldDo.when: It has been replaced with a business rule
architecture.proCodeWhereConfigWouldDo.then: The same fields show, hide, enable and require under the same conditions, and the script is no longer registered on the form
architecture.proCodeWhereConfigWouldDo.testRequirement: Walk every branch of the original script on the form. Business rules evaluate differently from an onload handler, particularly on a record that opens with the condition already met.

architecture.externalLogicInvisible.when: An owner and a repository have been recorded for what sits behind it
architecture.externalLogicInvisible.then: The architecture documentation names the service, its owner, its repository and what happens when it is unavailable
architecture.externalLogicInvisible.testRequirement: Confirm the recorded owner acknowledges it. An owner written down without being told is a name, not an owner.

quality.flowNoErrorHandling.then: The failure is reported to the agreed channel within one run, carrying the flow name, the run identifier and the failing action
quality.flowNoErrorHandling.testRequirement: Force a failure in a non production environment and confirm the notification arrives. A configure run after setting that points at nothing looks identical to a working one in the designer.

quality.flowFailureRate.given: The flow {componentName}, failing {evidenceValue} of its runs
quality.flowFailureRate.when: The cause has been found and fixed
quality.flowFailureRate.then: The failure rate over the following thirty days is below two percent, and any run that still fails does so for a reason somebody has written down
quality.flowFailureRate.testRequirement: Reproduce the original failure before fixing anything. A flow fixed without reproducing the failure is a flow that will fail again on the same input.

quality.flowSize.when: It has been split into child flows along the steps a person would describe out loud
quality.flowSize.then: No resulting flow exceeds forty actions, and each one has a name saying what it does rather than what it is part of
quality.flowSize.testRequirement: Run the whole chain end to end with the same trigger data as the original and compare the outcome. Splitting a flow changes the failure boundaries, so a child that fails now leaves the parent in a state the original never had.

quality.canvasDelegationWarnings.given: The canvas app {componentName}, with delegation warnings against {tableName}
quality.canvasDelegationWarnings.when: Each query over a table with real volume has been made delegable
quality.canvasDelegationWarnings.then: The app returns correct results against the full table, not only against the first five hundred rows
quality.canvasDelegationWarnings.testRequirement: Test against production volume, or a copy of it. Every one of these works in a development environment with two hundred rows, which is why the finding exists.

quality.pluginNoTracing.when: Tracing has been added at the entry and exit of each handler and at every branch that can throw
quality.pluginNoTracing.then: A failure in production leaves a trace log entry naming the handler, the branch and the record
quality.pluginNoTracing.testRequirement: Force an exception in a non production environment and read the trace log. Tracing that is written but never flushed, or written below the configured level, produces nothing and looks identical in the code.

quality.pluginNotSandboxed.given: The plugin assembly {componentName}, registered outside sandbox isolation
quality.pluginNotSandboxed.when: It has been rebuilt to run in sandbox isolation and registered in the database rather than on disk
quality.pluginNotSandboxed.then: It imports into an online environment, and the behaviour that needed full trust either works within the sandbox or has been moved outside the platform
quality.pluginNotSandboxed.testRequirement: Import into a clean environment and exercise every registered step. Expect to find at least one thing that needed full trust, because that is usually why it was registered this way.

quality.formScriptOnLoadWeight.when: Libraries are registered only on the forms that use them
quality.formScriptOnLoadWeight.then: Every form still behaves as it did, and the onload payload is smaller
quality.formScriptOnLoadWeight.testRequirement: Measure form load before and after, and exercise each form. A library removed from a form where a handler still references it fails at the point the user clicks something, not at load.

alm.unmanagedInProduction.given: Unmanaged customisations in the production environment {evidenceValue}
alm.unmanagedInProduction.when: A development environment is the source of truth and a pipeline promotes managed solutions into production
alm.unmanagedInProduction.then: No new unmanaged customisation appears in production, and what is there has been captured into a solution that can be exported
alm.unmanagedInProduction.testRequirement: Make a change in development, promote it, and confirm it arrives in production without anybody opening a maker portal there. Also confirm a change made directly in production is visible as an unmanaged layer, because that is how the next one gets caught.

alm.defaultSolutionComponents.given: {count} custom components whose only solution membership is the default solution
alm.defaultSolutionComponents.when: Each has been added to a named solution with a meaningful publisher prefix
alm.defaultSolutionComponents.then: An export of the named solutions carries every one of them, and an import into a clean environment produces a working application
alm.defaultSolutionComponents.testRequirement: Export and import into a clean environment and use the application. The components that get missed are the ones nothing visibly depends on until somebody runs the process that needs them.

alm.publisherPrefixSprawl.when: A prefix has been agreed for new work and written where a new developer will find it
alm.publisherPrefixSprawl.then: Components created after that date use the agreed prefix
alm.publisherPrefixSprawl.testRequirement: None on the existing components. Renaming a prefix is not something the platform permits, and attempting it is how a solution gets broken by a finding whose severity is low.

alm.missingConnectionReference.given: The flow {componentName}, carrying a connection rather than a connection reference
alm.missingConnectionReference.when: A connection reference exists per connector and the flow points at it
alm.missingConnectionReference.then: The solution imports into a second environment and the flow runs there after the reference is bound, with no edit to the flow itself
alm.missingConnectionReference.testRequirement: Import into an environment that has never held this solution and run the flow. Testing in an environment where the connection already exists proves nothing, because it resolves by accident.

alm.hardCodedEnvironmentValue.when: The value comes from an environment variable with no default
alm.hardCodedEnvironmentValue.then: The component resolves the value per environment, and an import into an environment where it is unset surfaces it as missing
alm.hardCodedEnvironmentValue.testRequirement: Import into a second environment with the variable unset and confirm it fails visibly rather than running against the wrong target. A default value shipped with the definition reproduces the original problem with more steps.

alm.environmentVariableWithDefault.given: The environment variable {componentName}, shipping a default value
alm.environmentVariableWithDefault.when: The default has been removed and the value is set per environment by the pipeline
alm.environmentVariableWithDefault.then: An import into an environment where the pipeline has not set it leaves the variable visibly empty
alm.environmentVariableWithDefault.testRequirement: Import into a clean environment and confirm the dependent component fails or warns rather than silently using the development value.

governance.orphanedColumn.given: {count} custom columns on {tableName} with no form, view, flow or plugin reference
governance.orphanedColumn.when: Each has been checked for integration traffic and a decision recorded
governance.orphanedColumn.then: Columns confirmed unused are deleted, and columns written by an integration are documented as such rather than deleted
governance.orphanedColumn.testRequirement: Check the audit history or API usage for writes to each column over a full business cycle before deleting any of them. This rule cannot see an integration, and its finding is a question rather than an instruction.

governance.securityRoleSprawl.given: The security role {componentName}, assigned to no user and no team
governance.securityRoleSprawl.when: It has been confirmed that nothing assigns it and it has been deleted
governance.securityRoleSprawl.then: The role no longer appears in the role picker
governance.securityRoleSprawl.testRequirement: Check whether a provisioning process assigns it on a schedule before deleting. A role assigned monthly by an automated job looks unassigned for twenty-nine days out of thirty.

security.organisationLevelWrite.given: The security role {componentName}, granting organisation level write on {tableName}
security.organisationLevelWrite.when: The privilege has been narrowed to business unit or user level
security.organisationLevelWrite.then: The people who hold the role can still do their work, and can no longer change records outside their scope
security.organisationLevelWrite.testRequirement: Have somebody who holds the role walk their actual daily tasks in a non production environment. Something will break, and finding out which thing in test is the entire purpose of this work item.

security.secretInDefinition.given: The {componentType} {componentName}, containing a credential in its definition
security.secretInDefinition.when: The credential has been rotated and the component reads it from Key Vault through an environment variable
security.secretInDefinition.then: The exported solution contains no credential, and the component works with the new one
security.secretInDefinition.testRequirement: Rotate first and confirm the old value stops working. Moving the secret without rotating leaves a live credential in every copy of the solution file that has already been exported, and in source control history.

governance.orphanedByOwner.given: The {componentType} {componentName}, owned by a disabled or absent user
governance.orphanedByOwner.when: Ownership has moved to a service principal or a solution owned by a group
governance.orphanedByOwner.then: The component runs on credentials that do not belong to one person, and its run history continues uninterrupted
governance.orphanedByOwner.testRequirement: Confirm the connections it uses were also reassigned. Changing the owner without changing the connections leaves it running on the departed person's authentication until that expires.

performance.plugSyncSlow.when: Work that does not need to be in the transaction has moved out of it
performance.plugSyncSlow.then: The average execution time is below five hundred milliseconds, and the behaviour that moved still happens
performance.plugSyncSlow.testRequirement: Measure the save time a user experiences, not the step duration in the trace. They are different numbers and the user only ever sees the first one.

performance.stepNoFilteringAttributes.given: The update step {componentName}, registered with no filtering attributes
performance.stepNoFilteringAttributes.when: The columns the handler actually reads are listed on the registration
performance.stepNoFilteringAttributes.then: The step no longer fires on changes to unrelated columns
performance.stepNoFilteringAttributes.testRequirement: Update a column outside the filter and confirm the handler does not run, then update one inside it and confirm it does. Getting the filter too narrow is as common as having none, and it fails silently in the other direction.

performance.viewComplexity.given: The default view {componentName} on {tableName}, with {count} columns or linked entities
performance.viewComplexity.when: The default view has been trimmed and the wide version kept as a named alternative
performance.viewComplexity.then: The table opens on a smaller default view and the wide view is still reachable
performance.viewComplexity.testRequirement: Confirm nothing depends on the default view's column set: an export, a template or a script reading the grid. Trimming a default view is the kind of change that breaks something a fortnight later.

operability.noFailureAlerting.given: The analysed solutions, with no component reporting a failure to a person
operability.noFailureAlerting.when: A failure path exists that reaches an agreed channel
operability.noFailureAlerting.then: A failure in any monitored component produces a message naming the component, the time and the identifier needed to find the run
operability.noFailureAlerting.testRequirement: Force a failure and confirm somebody receives it. Every other operability finding in this report assumes this one is done, so a notification that goes to an unmonitored mailbox invalidates the lot.

operability.noEnvironmentSeparation.given: The same solution present unmanaged in {count} environments with diverging versions
operability.noEnvironmentSeparation.when: One environment has been made the source and the others receive managed solutions from it
operability.noEnvironmentSeparation.then: A change made in the source environment reaches the others through a pipeline, and the divergence that existed has been reconciled and recorded
operability.noEnvironmentSeparation.testRequirement: Before anything else, produce a written comparison of what differs between the environments. Picking a source without knowing what the others have that it does not is how a fortnight of somebody's undocumented work disappears.

quality.namingInconsistent.when: A convention has been agreed and written where a new developer will find it
quality.namingInconsistent.then: Components created after that date follow it
quality.namingInconsistent.testRequirement: None on existing components. Renaming a schema name is not possible and renaming a display name breaks scripts, views and documentation that reference it, for a cosmetic gain.

quality.missingDescription.given: {count} custom {componentType} with no description in solution {solutionName}
quality.missingDescription.when: A description has been written saying what the component is for and who asked for it
quality.missingDescription.then: Somebody who has never seen the solution can tell what each one does from its description alone
quality.missingDescription.testRequirement: Have somebody outside the team read ten of them and say what each component does. A description repeating the display name passes every automated check and helps nobody.

performance.pcfBundleSize.given: The code component {componentName}, whose bundle is {sizeBytes} bytes
performance.pcfBundleSize.when: The bundle has been reduced, or the component replaced by something lighter
performance.pcfBundleSize.then: The form renders the same thing and downloads measurably less to do it
performance.pcfBundleSize.testRequirement: Measure the form load with the network throttled and the cache cold, before and after. A warm cache hides exactly the cost this is about.

modernisation.pcfBundlesOwnReact.given: The standard control {componentName}, bundling its own copy of React
modernisation.pcfBundlesOwnReact.when: It has been converted to a virtual control using the platform React library
modernisation.pcfBundlesOwnReact.then: It behaves as before and no longer ships a second React onto the form
modernisation.pcfBundlesOwnReact.testRequirement: Exercise every state of the control, not only the default one. Virtual controls render through the host, and a control that mutated the DOM directly will have a state where it stops doing so.

quality.pcfNotMinified.given: The code component {componentName}, shipped as unminified source
quality.pcfNotMinified.when: The solution carries a production build of it
quality.pcfNotMinified.then: The control behaves identically and the bundle is a fraction of the size
quality.pcfNotMinified.testRequirement: Confirm which build produced the deployed bundle, not only that a smaller one exists. The finding is usually that nobody knows.

quality.pcfDebugCodeShipped.given: The code component {componentName}, shipping debug code
quality.pcfDebugCodeShipped.then: The control behaves identically with developer tools open and closed
quality.pcfDebugCodeShipped.testRequirement: Open the browser developer tools and use the control. A debugger statement does nothing at all until somebody does that, which is why it survives testing.

performance.pcfPollingTimer.given: The code component {componentName}, which starts {timerCount} timer(s) when it loads
performance.pcfPollingTimer.when: Each timer has been justified, or replaced, and every one that remains is cleared in destroy
performance.pcfPollingTimer.then: Closing the form stops all work the control was doing, and no timer outlives it
performance.pcfPollingTimer.testRequirement: Open the form, close it, and watch for the timer firing afterwards. Leave a form open for an hour and check memory. Thirty seconds of testing is exactly the interval in which this behaves perfectly.

security.pcfInnerHtml.given: The code component {componentName}, which assigns to innerHTML in {innerHtmlCount} place(s)
security.pcfInnerHtml.when: Every assignment carrying record data has been changed to escape it
security.pcfInnerHtml.then: The control renders identically and record data can no longer become markup
security.pcfInnerHtml.testRequirement: Put a script tag in one of the fields the control reads and open the form. Test the fields it reads indirectly too, not only the ones it is bound to.

quality.pcfUndeclaredWebApi.given: The code component {componentName}, calling the Web API without declaring the feature
quality.pcfUndeclaredWebApi.when: The manifest declares WebAPI feature usage and the rebuilt control is deployed
quality.pcfUndeclaredWebApi.then: Every path through the control that calls the Web API completes instead of throwing
quality.pcfUndeclaredWebApi.testRequirement: Exercise the paths that actually make the call, not the form load. The control loads fine today, which is the whole problem.
